schemaNotes.signalChain: Array of channel/element objects, each with an ordered array of processing steps (mic -> preamp -> EQ -> compression -> saturation -> reverb/delay, etc).
schemaNotes.step.step: 1-based order position of this processor within its channel chain.
schemaNotes.step.processorType: Category of processor, e.g. Microphone, Preamp, EQ, Compression, De-essing / Saturation, Reverb, Delay.
schemaNotes.step.product: Specific hardware unit or plugin used at this step.
schemaNotes.step.settings: The exact parameter settings applied (ratios, frequencies, times, wet/dry, etc).
schemaNotes.step.why: Engineering rationale explaining why this processor/setting was chosen at this point in the chain.

steps.why: Standard in Detroit/LA rap sessions; captures chest and consonant attack for rapid delivery
Adds harmonic density and weight without harshness; cleans low rumble

steps.settings: 2-3 dB boost 3-4 kHz presence, gentle cut 300 Hz
steps.why: Pushes intelligibility forward through dense low-mid beat
Controls dynamic range of aggressive rap without killing punch; vintage saturation
Tames sibilance; subtle harmonic excitement maintains presence
Room ambience without washing dry upfront vocal
Warm detailed pickup for sung R&B-inflected hook
Preserves body and warmth to contrast punchy rap

steps.settings: 2 dB boost 10 kHz, 1 dB boost 100 Hz
steps.why: Classic air boost opens top end above instrumental
Opens hook spatially, separates from drier rap
MPC-style chopped loop standard for West Coast hip-hop

steps.settings: HP 40 Hz, cut 200-250 Hz 2-3 dB, boost 8-10 kHz 1.5 dB
steps.why: Clears low-mid muddiness; restores air from sampling
Glues loop into drum texture; SSL pumping defined era
Restores analog warmth from digital sampling
Vintage glue so sample feels real

steps.settings: Kick 55-60 Hz, snare layered body+crack, hats 1/8th
steps.why: MPC standard for Aftermath/Shady; layering builds punch

steps.settings: Boost 60 Hz sub, 4 kHz click, cut 200-300 Hz
steps.why: Hit on speakers and earbuds — weight plus attack

steps.settings: Fast attack, medium release, 8:1, 8-10 dB GR smashed
steps.why: Cracking punchy snare snaps through dense mix
NY-style density without killing dry snap

steps.settings: Long decay, full sustain, tuned to root
Boost 50-60 Hz 3 dB, HP <35 Hz, cut 200-400 Hz
steps.why: Focuses sub energy; prevents low-mid muddiness

artists.sunoPrompt: Hard-hitting early 2000s hip-hop track with dusty looped soul sample, deep sub-bass, cracking dry snare, dry upfront rap with fast-attack compression. Sparse heavy low end and punchy midrange. Dark aggressive energy, radio-ready major-label feel.
artists.mixBusNotes: Dry punchy front-loaded housts and drums upfront with minimal reverb wash, for a direct, polished hip-hop balance. Master bus: SSL G-Bus glue (2:1, slow attack, ~3 dB GR) then Neve/Manley shelf polish. Stereo moderate and controlled — kick, bass, lead vocal mono center; sample loop and reverb tails provide spread.

steps.why: SM7B provides a focused vocal tone; U87 adds detail for sung passages
Analog character without over-coloring intimate vocal

steps.settings: Boost 3-4 kHz presence, gentle cut 250 Hz, shelf 12 kHz air
steps.why: Clarifies rapid syllables; air shelf lifts sung verses

steps.settings: 4:1, medium attack, medium release, 5-7 dB GR
steps.why: Controls dynamic shifts between sung and rapped passages
Tames sibilance in high-register sung parts
Spacious emotional atmosphere for ballad vibe
Rhythmic echoes fill space around melodic phrases
Consistent with lead for tonal cohesion

steps.settings: Air 10 kHz +2 dB, body 100 Hz +1 dB

steps.why: Keeps backing vocals even and warm
Creates depth and separation behind lead
Real piano samples provide organic warmth

steps.settings: HP 60 Hz, cut 200 Hz 2 dB, boost 8 kHz 1 dB

steps.why: Blend of programmed and live drums

steps.settings: Boost 60 Hz, 3 kHz click, cut 250 Hz
Boost 50-60 Hz 3 dB, HP <35 Hz, cut 200-400 Hz

artists.sunoPrompt: Melodic rap ballad with rich piano loop, spacious drums, polished emotional vocal blending singing and rapping. Deep sub-bass, shimmering piano, warm reverb create cinematic atmosphere. Modern major-label production with intimate vocal presence.
artists.mixBusNotes: Polished and spacious - lead vocal intimate front-center with moderate hall reverb and rhythmic delays. Drums punchy but not aggressive. Piano loop and sub-bass fill low end. Stereo wider than classic hip-hop; piano and reverb spread wide while kick, vocal, bass stay centered. Master bus: SSL G-Bus 2:1 ~4 dB, subtle shelf EQ for shimmer and sub weight.
